C08 and C03 are also very close templates, but their wording uses the plural \"conditions,\" making C21 the strongest textual match.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"WHEREAS a dispute exists between the Reading Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Organization of Masters, Mates and Pilots, Local No. 14, a labor organization","parent_excerpt":"WHEREAS a dispute exists between the Trans World Airlines, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO, a labor organization","explanation":"The same party-identification sentence structure is reused with the disputing carrier and union substituted."},{"child_excerpt":"WHEREAS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and WHEREAS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential transportation service","explanation":"The two substantive predicates appear verbatim and in the same sequence."},{"child_excerpt":"The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.","parent_excerpt":"The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.","explanation":"The reporting obligation is verbatim."},{"child_excerpt":"As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by The Reading Company or by its employees, in the condition out of which the dispute arose.","parent_excerpt":"As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the Trans World Airlines, Inc. or by its employees, in the condition out of which the dispute arose.","explanation":"The operative status-quo provision is nearly verbatim, including the singular \"condition\"; only the carrier name and immaterial punctuation/capitalization differ."}]}
